explanation: This recursively force-deletes the entire filesystem starting at /. It would destroy the operating system and all data on the server. Never run this, with or without sudo.
This recursively force-deletes everything starting from the root of the filesystem -- the flag order doesn't make it any safer.
This deletes the user's entire home directory and everything in it, with no way to undo it.
dd writing to a raw disk device overwrites it byte-for-byte, permanently destroying the partition table and all data on that disk.
This is a fork bomb. It spawns processes exponentially until the system runs out of memory and CPU, effectively crashing it for everyone.
This makes every file on the entire system world-readable, writable and executable -- a critical, system-wide security failure, not a fix for one file's permissions.
mkfs formats a filesystem, erasing everything on that disk. Only ever run this on a disk you intend to wipe, never on a live system disk.
Redirecting output directly onto a disk device overwrites its raw contents and destroys the data on it, the same as dd would.
This powers off the server immediately. Even during an incident, a shutdown should be a deliberate, announced action -- not a reflex fix for a failed service.
